claim: The water molecule between the sidechain of Asp130 and Tl+ indicates that the bound substrate ion retains part of its hydration shell.
source: The water molecule between the sidechain of Asp130 and Tl+ indicates that the bound substrate ion retains part of its hydration shell, as complete dehydration is energetically unfavourable.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observation.

claim: In PaNhaP, all ion-binding residues are found in the first half of the inverted repeat.
source: In PaNhaP, all ion-binding residues are found in the first half of the inverted repeat.
evidence: This structural observation is explicitly stated.

claim: The structure and interaction of the ion-coordinating Asp159 and Ser155 in H6 resemble those of the inversely oriented Glu408 and Ser404 in H13 in the second half of the inverted repeat.
source: Interestingly, the structure and interaction of the ion-coordinating Asp159 and Ser155 in H6 resemble those of the inversely oriented Glu408 and Ser404 in H13 in the second half of the inverted repeat (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: This structural similarity is described and shown in figures.

claim: An early form of the CPA1 antiporters may have had a second, symmetrical ion-binding site that has been lost in the course of evolution.
source: This may imply that an early form of the CPA1 antiporters, which must have arisen by gene duplication of an unknown precursor, had a second, symmetrical ion-binding site that has been lost in the course of evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative evolutionary interpretation.

claim: Arg362 in the unwound stretch of H12 is essential in MjNhaP1.
source: Arg362 in the unwound stretch of H12, which is essential in MjNhaP1 (Hellmer et al., 2003) and completely conserved in the CPA1 antiporters (Hellmer et al., 2003; Goswami et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Arg362 is completely conserved in the CPA1 antiporters.
source: and completely conserved in the CPA1 antiporters (Hellmer et al., 2003; Goswami et al., 2011)
evidence: This conservation is stated with citations.

claim: Arg362 may be a tethered positive charge that takes the place of the Na+ ion in the second half of the inverted repeat.
source: may be a tethered positive charge that takes the place of the Na+ ion in the second half of the inverted repeat, in a way similar to the arginine that replaces the co-transported Na+ in the sodium-independent substrate/product antiporter CaiT (Kalayil et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with a citation to a similar case.

claim: The transport activity of PaNhaP is highest at pH 5 and declines at higher or lower pH.
source: The transport activity of PaNhaP is highest at pH 5 and declines at higher or lower pH.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental data.

claim: The bell-shaped pH profile is explained in terms of the Na+ affinity of the acidic residues in the substrate-binding pocket.
source: The resulting bell-shaped pH profile is explained in terms of the Na+ affinity of the acidic residues in the substrate-binding pocket.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the pH profile.

claim: The protonation state of the ion-coordinating carboxyl sidechains is likely to affect the affinity of the binding site for Na+.
source: The protonation state of these is likely to affect the affinity of the binding site for Na+.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation.

claim: At low pH, most if not all of the ion-coordinating carboxyl sidechains would be protonated, resulting in reduced affinity for Na+.
source: At low pH, most if not all of the ion-coordinating carboxyl sidechains (Glu73, Asp130, and Asp159) would be protonated, resulting in reduced affinity for Na+, as has been shown for MjNhaP1 by electrophysiological measurements on solid-supported membranes (Calinescu et al., 2014).
evidence: This interpretation is stated with a citation to supporting data.

claim: At pH > 7, the ion-binding site is predominantly deprotonated and negatively charged, resulting in an increased Na+ affinity.
source: At pH > 7, the ion-binding site is predominantly deprotonated and negatively charged (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), resulting in an increased Na+ affinity.
evidence: This interpretation is stated and supported by a figure.

claim: Increased Na+ affinity at high pH would result in decreased transport rate, as the ions are bound more tightly.
source: As a result, the transport rate would decrease, as the ions are bound more tightly.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation.

claim: The increased transport rate of the E73A mutant is consistent with one less carboxyl in the binding site, hence easier Na+ release.
source: This is consistent with the increased transport rate of the E73A mutant, which has one less carboxyl in the binding site, hence releases Na+ more easily (Figure 8B).
evidence: This interpretation is stated and supported by experimental data.

claim: The pH-dependent transport activity of PaNhaP suggests a self-regulatory mechanism for the binding site.
source: The pH-dependent transport activity of PaNhaP suggests a self-regulatory mechanism for the binding site rather than regulation by a separate pH sensor as proposed for EcNhaA (Herz et al., 2010; Diab et al., 2011; Schushan et al., 2012).
evidence: This interpretation is stated with citations to alternative mechanisms.

claim: At the pH 5 activity maximum of PaNhaP, transport is not limited by Na+ affinity.
source: At the pH 5 activity maximum of PaNhaP, transport is not limited by Na+ affinity.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the kinetic data.

claim: Cooperative ion binding is most likely mediated by Glu73.
source: Cooperative ion binding is most likely mediated by Glu73
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation.

claim: Cooperative increase in Na+ affinity at neutral or basic pH may be important for controlling the intracellular pH.
source: and may be important for controlling the intracellular pH at neutral or basic pH, where a cooperative increase in Na+ affinity would gradually inhibit substrate release and slow down transport
evidence: This is a functional interpretation.

claim: Cooperativity may be a safety mechanism to protect the organism against excessive influx of Na+ at rising pH.
source: This may be a safety mechanism to protect the organism against excessive influx of Na+, and hence efflux of protons, at rising pH, which may be critical for survival.
evidence: This is a speculative functional interpretation.

claim: The human Na+/H+ exchanger NHE1 is a dimer.
source: The medically relevant but elusive human Na+/H+ exchanger NHE1 is a dimer (Fafournoux et al., 1994) like PaNhaP.
evidence: This is stated with a citation.

claim: PaNhaP and NHE1 share high sequence homology.
source: Several other common features, including high sequence homology (Goswami et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated with a citation.

claim: NHE1 also shows pH-dependent Na+ cooperativity, with a Hill coefficient of 1.8 at pH 6.8 that drops to ∼1 at pH 6.
source: Remarkably, NHE1 also shows pH-dependent Na+ cooperativity, with a Hill coefficient of 1.8 at pH 6.8 that drops to ∼1 at pH 6 (Fuster et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation.

claim: The PaNhaP structure serves as an excellent model for the membrane part of NHE1.
source: The PaNhaP structure thus serves as an excellent model for the membrane part of NHE1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the similarities.

claim: Molecular details of allosteric regulation in NHE1 are likely to be different, as the His292 is not conserved.
source: Molecular details of allosteric regulation in NHE1 are likely to be different, as the His292 that reorients in response to pH in PaNhaP is not conserved (Goswami et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation.

claim: The electrogenic CPA2 antiporters have two conserved aspartates in place of the ND motif in H6.
source: The electrogenic CPA2 antiporters, such as EcNhaA or TtNapA, which exchange two protons against one Na+, have two conserved aspartates in place of the ND motif in H6.
evidence: This sequence difference is explicitly stated.

claim: TtNapA is more similar to PaNhaP than to EcNhaA in terms of overall structure.
source: In terms of its overall structure, TtNapA (Lee et al., 2013) is more similar to PaNhaP than to EcNhaA (Hunte et al., 2005), especially with respect to the dimer interface.
evidence: This comparison is stated with citations.

claim: The tertiary structure of the CPA antiporters is not a diagnostic of electroneutral or electrogenic transport.
source: The tertiary structure of the CPA antiporters is thus not a diagnostic of electroneutral or electrogenic transport.
evidence: This conclusion is stated based on structural comparisons.

claim: In Pyrococcus, the Na+ gradient required for ATP synthesis is maintained by specific antiporters.
source: In Pyrococcus, the Na+ gradient required for ATP synthesis is maintained by specific antiporters (McTernan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation.

claim: PaNhaP utilizes the Na+ gradient across the membrane for pH homeostasis.
source: We therefore assume that PaNhaP, like human NHE1, utilizes the Na+ gradient across the membrane (Cohen et al., 2003) for pH homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as an assumption with a citation.

claim: Protons can reach the binding pocket either through the cytoplasmic funnel or through the narrow polar channel.
source: Protons, probably in the form of hydronium ions (H3O+), can reach the binding pocket either through the cytoplasmic funnel or through the narrow polar channel (Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated as a mechanistic possibility shown in a figure.

claim: Using the second narrow polar channel for proton translocation would physically separate the routes for Na+ and H3O+ on the cytoplasmic side.
source: Using the second narrow polar channel for proton translocation would physically separate the routes for Na+ and H3O+ on the cytoplasmic side, which may be an advantage as the two ion currents flow in opposite directions.
evidence: This is a speculative functional interpretation.

claim: The conservation of residues lining the narrow polar channel suggests it may be used for proton translocation.
source: It would also explain why residues that line this channel, in particular the Glu154/Arg337 ion bridge and Asn158, which do not participate in ion coordination, are so highly conserved in the family.
evidence: This is an inference based on conservation patterns.

claim: The rmsd between the structures at pH 8 and pH 4 is 1.57 Å.
source: The rmsd between the structures at pH 8 and pH 4 is 1.57 Å.
evidence: This structural comparison metric is explicitly stated.
